newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Stay cautious on India-ING Barings.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Stay cautious on India-ING Barings.

text.p: Securities firm ING Barings on Thursday warned investors they must be cautious with first quarter 1997 allocations for India.
In a December strategy piece titled, "Where Angels Fear to Tread," ING Barings said the Indian economy was poised for a shakeout similar to the one witnessed in the early nineties.
"The balance of payments crisis has been replaced by an internal debt trap," the securities house said.
"The gross fiscal deficit this year will be among the highest of the decade and the majority of state governments will be facing their worst financial crisis."
ING Barings said these issues needed bold economic reforms over the next two years and could not be resolved by merely tinkering with the monetary policy.
It said a slowdown in demand coupled with a gloomy capital market and rapidly expanding capacities in most industries would lead to shrinking corporate profitability.

"We believe the market has sensed the impending danger in economic and corporate performance but has not sufficiently discounted it due to a lack of conclusive evidence..it is still skidding and in the process of forming a long-term bottom," the report said.
It advised investors to delay further investments until the grim realities in the capital market environment were adequately factored in.

"We recommend emerging market asset allocators to critically review their past India investment theories and portfolio performance and be cautious with first quarter 1997 asset allocations," ING Barings said.
